### Phase 0 & 1 — Protocol Vocabulary, Trust Boundaries, and Entry Point Audit

We start from the Money Map and work through **Lens 9 — Access, Authorization & Trust Boundaries** across [RaffleFactory.sol](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol) and [Raffle.sol](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol).

---

### Lifecycle 1 — Creation & Escrow (`RaffleFactory::createRaffle` → `Raffle::initialize` → `Raffle::onERC721Received`)

[Model: RaffleFactory::createRaffle]
A sponsor supplies a prize NFT, a sponsor payout recipient, a reserve entry threshold, and an end time. The factory increments `raffleCount`, deploys a new clone of `raffleImplementation`, initializes the clone in `AwaitingPrize` status, registers the clone in `raffleById`, `idByRaffle`, and `isRaffle`, pulls the prize NFT from the caller into the clone (which transitions the clone to `Active`), and checks that the clone now owns the NFT and is `Active`.

[Model: Raffle::initialize]
Called once by `factory` on a fresh clone. It records the sponsor, `sponsorRecipient`, `protocolTreasury`, `prizeToken`, `prizeTokenId`, `raffleId`, `reserveEntries`, and `endTime`, screens `sponsor`, `protocolTreasury`, and `sponsorRecipient` against known protocol addresses, sets `initialized = true`, and sets `status = Status.AwaitingPrize`.

[Model: Raffle::onERC721Received]
Called by `prizeToken` when the prize NFT is transferred into the raffle clone. It verifies that `status == Status.AwaitingPrize`, the caller is `prizeToken`, the token ID is `prizeTokenId`, the previous owner `from` is `sponsor`, and the transfer `operator` is `factory`, then transitions `status` to `Status.Active`.

[Why: Raffle.sol:615]
Why does [`_isProtocolDestination`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L606-L618) only check `canonicalFactory.isRaffle(destination)` when `destination.code.length != 0`, and why does it assume `isRaffle(destination)` is static over a raffle's lifetime?
The code rests on the implicit belief that every `Raffle` clone that could ever be passed as a `destination` (`sponsorRecipient`, `protocolTreasury`, or a ticket `recipient`/`to`) is already deployed and registered in `isRaffle` at the moment the check runs. However, [`RaffleFactory::createRaffle`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol#L739) deploys clones via `Clones.clone(raffleImplementation)`, which uses `CREATE` from `address(factory)` with a predictable sequential nonce (`nonce = raffleCount + 1`, where nonce `1` was `raffleImplementation`). Before future clone `R_next` is deployed, `R_next.code.length == 0` and `isRaffle[R_next] == false`, so `R_next` passes [`_isProtocolDestination`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L606-L618) during `initialize` and `_update`, and only becomes a registered `isRaffle` clone with `code.length > 0` after the subsequent `createRaffle` call.

[Defeat: Raffle::_isProtocolDestination]
1. Attacker computes the deterministic `CREATE` address of the next clone `R2 = computeCreateAddress(factory, raffleCount + 2)` while `R1` is active (`R2.code.length == 0`, `isRaffle[R2] == false`), and calls `R1.buyEntries(R2, 1)` (or `R1.transferFrom(attacker, R2, ticketId)`). `_isProtocolDestination(R2, address(prizeToken))` returns `false` and `ERC721Utils.checkOnERC721Received` skips the callback because `R2.code.length == 0`. When any sponsor later calls `factory.createRaffle(...)`, `R2` is deployed at `R2` (`isRaffle[R2] = true`), leaving a registered `Raffle` clone owning a ticket in `R1` (violating Invariant 9) that can never be redeemed or refunded.
2. A sponsor creates `R1` with `sponsorRecipient = R2` (the next deterministic `CREATE` address of `factory`). At creation time `R2` passes both [`RaffleFactory::_validateCreateParams`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol#L796-L802) and [`Raffle::initialize`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L206-L208). Once `R2` is deployed, `R1.releaseSponsorProceeds()` permanently reverts with `InvalidQuoteDestination(R2)` in [`_transferQuote`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L577-L580), whereas [`R1.releaseSponsorPrize()`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L408-L420) omits `_isProtocolDestination` and transfers the prize NFT via `transferFrom` directly into `R2`, moving an asset between raffle clones and stranding it in `R2`.
3. A deployer configures `protocolTreasury` in [`RaffleFactory::constructor`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol#L698-L725) to a deterministic future clone address `R_k`; raffles `1 .. k-1` initialize cleanly, and once raffle `k` is created at `R_k`, `releaseProtocolFees()` on all earlier raffles reverts with `InvalidQuoteDestination(R_k)` and raffle `k` and all future raffles revert in `initialize` with `UnsafeProtocolDestination(R_k)`.

[Defeat: RaffleFactory::createRaffle]
1. Malicious `sponsor` deploys an untrusted `prizeToken` (which `DESIGN.md` explicitly classifies as untrusted: *"arbitrary prize contracts and ticket recipients are untrusted"*) that implements `supportsInterface(0x80ac58cd) == true`, calls `raffle.onERC721Received(factory, sponsor, prizeTokenId, "")` during `safeTransferFrom`, and reports `ownerOf(prizeTokenId) == raffle` during `createRaffle`, but reverts in `transferFrom(raffle, winner, prizeTokenId)` once `status == Status.NftWon`.
2. Inside `prize.safeTransferFrom(msg.sender, raffle, params.prizeTokenId)` at [`RaffleFactory.sol:761`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol#L761), after calling [`Raffle::onERC721Received`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L429-L444) (which has no `nonReentrant` modifier and sets `status = Status.Active`), `prizeToken` calls `raffle.buyEntries(attacker, 10)` before `createRaffle` finishes. `status` remains `Status.Active`, so `createRaffle` succeeds while `TicketPurchased` is emitted before `RaffleCreated`.
3. `prizeToken` attempts to call `raffle.enableRefunds()` as `sponsor` during `safeTransferFrom` after `onERC721Received` sets `status = Status.Active`; this transitions `raffle.status()` to `Status.Refunding`, which is caught by `if (IRaffle(raffle).status() != IRaffle.Status.Active) revert PrizeEscrowVerificationFailed(...)` at [`RaffleFactory.sol:765`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/RaffleFactory.sol#L765).

[LastOut: Lifecycle 1 — Creation & Escrow]
At the end of `createRaffle`, no USDC has entered `Raffle` (`unsettledPot == 0`, `accountedQuoteBalance() == 0`), and `prizeToken.ownerOf(prizeTokenId) == raffle`. If zero entries are sold and `enableRefunds()` is called, `releaseSponsorPrize()` returns `prizeTokenId` to `sponsorRecipient` in full (unless `sponsorRecipient` was set to a future `Raffle` clone or blocks ERC-721 transfers).

---

### Lifecycle 2 — Entry Purchase (`Raffle::buyEntries` & `Raffle::_update`)

[Model: Raffle::buyEntries]
A buyer specifies a ticket `recipient` and `entryCount` while the raffle is `Active` and before `endTime`. The contract pulls `entryCount * 1,000,000` quote tokens from `msg.sender`, advances `totalEntries` by `entryCount`, increments `ticketCount`, records `[firstEntry, lastEntry]` in `_ticketRanges[ticketId]`, adds `grossAmount` to `unsettledPot`, and mints sequential ticket `ticketId` to `recipient`.

[Model: Raffle::_update]
Called on every ticket mint, transfer, or burn. When `to != address(0)`, it checks `_isProtocolDestination(to, address(prizeToken))` to reject protocol plumbing addresses, then updates ERC-721 ownership and balances.

[LastOut: Lifecycle 2 — Entry Purchase]
Every entry purchase adds `grossAmount = entryCount * 1,000,000` USDC to `quoteToken.balanceOf(address(this))` and increases `unsettledPot` by the exact same `grossAmount`. `unsettledPot == uint256(totalEntries) * 1,000,000 == quoteToken.balanceOf(address(this))`, so 100% of purchased entries are backed 1:1 by USDC in the contract.

---

### Lifecycle 3 — Draw & Resolution (`Raffle::requestDraw` → `Raffle::fulfillRandomWords`)

[Model: Raffle::requestDraw]
Any caller in `[endTime, drawRequestDeadline())` when `totalEntries > 0` supplies native ETH to cover the Chainlink VRF v2.5 wrapper fee. The raffle sets `status = Status.Drawing`, records `drawRequestedAt = uint64(block.timestamp)`, sets `_requestInFlight = true`, pays `paidPrice` in native ETH to `i_vrfV2PlusWrapper`, stores `vrfRequestId`, clears `_requestInFlight`, and refunds `msg.value - paidPrice` in native ETH to `msg.sender`.

[Model: Raffle::fulfillRandomWords]
Called by `i_vrfV2PlusWrapper` via `rawFulfillRandomWords`. If `_requestInFlight` is false, `status == Status.Drawing`, `requestId == vrfRequestId`, `randomWords.length == 1`, and `block.timestamp < callbackDeadline()`, it computes `winningEntry = uint128((randomWords[0] % uint256(totalEntries)) + 1)`, records `resolvedAt`, and transitions `status` to `Status.NftWon` (if `totalEntries >= reserveEntries`) or `Status.CashWon` (otherwise).

[Why: Raffle.sol:267]
Why does [`requestDraw`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L267-L273) set `_requestInFlight = true` before `requestRandomnessPayInNative` and clear it only after writing `vrfRequestId = requestId`?
Because `rawFulfillRandomWords` is not `nonReentrant`, and `vrfRequestId` is only returned by `requestRandomWordsInNative` after the external call to the wrapper finishes; without `_requestInFlight`, a synchronous callback from a wrapper before `vrfRequestId` is written would see `vrfRequestId == 0`.

[Defeat: Raffle::requestDraw]
1. Attacker deploys a helper contract with a `receive()` function that reverts, and calls `requestDraw()` with `msg.value = quotedFee + 1 wei`. The native refund at [`Raffle.sol:280`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L280-L282) reverts with `NativeRefundFailed`, reverting the entire `requestDraw()` call so the raffle stays in `Status.Active` and another caller can still call `requestDraw()`.
2. Attacker force-sends 1 ETH to `Raffle` via `selfdestruct` before `requestDraw()`, then calls `requestDraw()` with `msg.value == quotedFee`. `requestRandomnessPayInNative` forwards only `{value: requestPrice}` to `i_vrfV2PlusWrapper` and refunds `msg.value - paidPrice` (`0`), leaving the force-sent 1 ETH harmlessly ignored.
3. Attacker calls `rawFulfillRandomWords` directly to forge a winning entry; [`VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase::rawFulfillRandomWords`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/node_modules/@chainlink/contracts/src/v0.8/vrf/dev/VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.sol#L101-L107) checks `if (msg.sender != vrfWrapperAddr) revert OnlyVRFWrapperCanFulfill(msg.sender, vrfWrapperAddr)`.

[LastOut: Lifecycle 3 — Draw & Resolution]
During `requestDraw` and `fulfillRandomWords`, no USDC enters or leaves `Raffle` (`unsettledPot` remains `totalEntries * 1,000,000`), and the draw requester receives `msg.value - paidPrice` back in the same transaction while `paidPrice` is transferred to `i_vrfV2PlusWrapper`.

---

### Lifecycle 4 — Settlement & Claims (`settleWinningTicket`, `redeemWinningTicket`, `releaseSponsorProceeds`, `releaseProtocolFees`, `releaseSponsorPrize`)

[Model: Raffle::_settleWinningTicket]
Anyone passes `ticketId` after the raffle resolves to `NftWon` or `CashWon`. The contract verifies `winningEntry` lies within `_ticketRanges[ticketId]`, zeroes `unsettledPot`, sets `settlementComplete = true` and `winningTicketId = ticketId`, allocates 5% of `grossPot` (rounded down) to `protocolFees`, allocates 80% of `grossPot` (rounded down) to `winnerProceeds` if `CashWon` (or 0 if `NftWon`), and allocates the remaining `grossPot` to `sponsorProceeds`.

[Model: Raffle::redeemWinningTicket]
The current owner of `winningTicketId` calls `redeemWinningTicket(ticketId)` in `NftWon` or `CashWon`. It settles the winning ticket first if not yet settled, verifies `msg.sender == ownerOf(ticketId)`, sets `winnerRecipient = winner` and `winnerRedeemed = true`, burns `ticketId`, and either transfers `prizeTokenId` to `winner` (in `NftWon`, setting `prizeClaimed = true` and checking `prizeToken.ownerOf(prizeTokenId) == winner`) or zeroes `winnerProceeds` and transfers that USDC amount to `winner` (in `CashWon`).

[Model: Raffle::releaseSponsorProceeds]
Anyone calls `releaseSponsorProceeds()`. It reads `sponsorProceeds`, reverts if zero, zeroes `sponsorProceeds`, and transfers that USDC amount to `sponsorRecipient`.

[Model: Raffle::releaseProtocolFees]
Anyone calls `releaseProtocolFees()`. It reads `protocolFees`, reverts if zero, zeroes `protocolFees`, and transfers that USDC amount to `protocolTreasury`.

[Model: Raffle::releaseSponsorPrize]
Anyone calls `releaseSponsorPrize()` when `status` is `CashWon` or `Refunding` and `prizeClaimed` is false. It sets `prizeClaimed = true`, transfers `prizeTokenId` from the raffle to `sponsorRecipient`, and verifies `prizeToken.ownerOf(prizeTokenId) == sponsorRecipient`.

[Model: Raffle::_transferQuote]
Checks that `to` is not a protocol destination via `_isProtocolDestination(to, address(prizeToken))`, then transfers `amount` of `quoteToken` to `to`.

[Why: Raffle.sol:388]
Why does [`releaseSponsorProceeds`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L388-L395) allow releasing `sponsorProceeds` (95% of the gross USDC pot in `Status.NftWon`) as soon as [`_settleWinningTicket`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L546-L571) completes, without requiring `prizeClaimed == true` (or verifying that `prizeToken` can still be transferred to the winner)?
The code rests on the implicit belief that because `prizeToken` transferred into `Raffle` during `createRaffle`, `prizeToken.transferFrom(address(this), winner, prizeTokenId)` is guaranteed to succeed later in `redeemWinningTicket`. However, `DESIGN.md` explicitly specifies that *"arbitrary prize contracts and ticket recipients are untrusted"*, and even standards-compliant ERC-721 tokens can expire (e.g., ENS names expiring during the up-to-34-day raffle lifecycle), be paused, or enforce creator/transfer restrictions. Because `_settleWinningTicket` is storage-only and `releaseSponsorProceeds` does not check `prizeClaimed` in `Status.NftWon`, a sponsor with a malicious, paused, or expired `prizeToken` can settle and withdraw 95% of all buyers' USDC in `Status.NftWon` while `redeemWinningTicket` permanently reverts for the winner.

[Why: Raffle.sol:417]
Why do [`releaseSponsorPrize`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L417) and [`redeemWinningTicket`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L347) transfer `prizeToken` without calling `_isProtocolDestination`, whereas [`_transferQuote`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L577-L580) re-screens `to` with `_isProtocolDestination`?
The code assumes `sponsorRecipient` and `winner` were already screened at `initialize` and `_update` time and cannot become protocol destinations later. Because future `Raffle` clones are created via `CREATE` and registered in `isRaffle` after earlier raffles are initialized, `sponsorRecipient` can become a registered `isRaffle` clone after `initialize`, allowing `releaseSponsorPrize` to transfer the prize NFT directly into another `Raffle` clone via `transferFrom`.

[Defeat: Raffle::redeemWinningTicket]
1. Sponsor creates a raffle with an untrusted `prizeToken` (which `DESIGN.md` explicitly marks as untrusted) that blocks `transferFrom` when `status == Status.NftWon` (or an expiring ERC-721 such as an ENS name that expires before redemption). Once `totalEntries >= reserveEntries` and VRF resolves to `Status.NftWon`, the sponsor calls `settleWinningTicket(winningTicketId)` and `releaseSponsorProceeds()` to extract 95% of the USDC pot, while `redeemWinningTicket(winningTicketId)` permanently reverts on `prizeToken.transferFrom`, leaving the winning ticket holder with neither the NFT nor any USDC refund.
2. Attacker attempts to call `settleWinningTicket(wrongTicketId)` with a non-winning ticket ID to lock `winningTicketId` to their own ticket; [`_requireWinningTicket`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L592-L598) checks `selectedEntry < firstEntry || selectedEntry > lastEntry` and reverts with `TicketDoesNotContainWinningEntry`.
3. If `winner` is blacklisted by USDC in `Status.CashWon` or blocked by `prizeToken` in `Status.NftWon`, `winner` transfers `winningTicketId` to an unblocked EOA `winnerAlt` via `transferFrom(winner, winnerAlt, winningTicketId)` before calling `redeemWinningTicket(winningTicketId)`, and `winnerAlt` redeems.

[LastOut: Lifecycle 4 — Settlement & Claims]
For `totalEntries >= 1`, `grossPot = totalEntries * 1,000,000`.
- In `Status.NftWon`: `protocolFee = floor(grossPot * 500 / 10,000) = totalEntries * 50,000` and `sponsorAmount = grossPot - protocolFee = totalEntries * 950,000`. `protocolFee + sponsorAmount == grossPot`. Both `releaseProtocolFees()` and `releaseSponsorProceeds()` get paid in full down to the last wei of USDC; however, if `prizeToken` is untrusted/paused/expired, `sponsor` and `protocolTreasury` withdraw 100% of the USDC while the last claimant (`winner` calling `redeemWinningTicket`) reverts and receives neither the NFT nor USDC.
- In `Status.CashWon`: `protocolFee = totalEntries * 50,000`, `cashAmount = totalEntries * 800,000`, and `sponsorAmount = grossPot - protocolFee - cashAmount = totalEntries * 150,000`. `protocolFee + cashAmount + sponsorAmount == grossPot`, so all three cohorts (`winner`, `sponsorRecipient`, `protocolTreasury`) are paid in full with zero shortfall.

### Lifecycle 5 — Refund Lifecycle (`enableRefunds` → `refundTickets` + `releaseSponsorPrize`)

[Model: Raffle::enableRefunds]
Transitions the raffle to `Status.Refunding` when a liveness deadline expires (`drawRequestDeadline()` in `Status.Active` with `totalEntries > 0`, `callbackDeadline()` in `Status.Drawing`, or `endTime` / `msg.sender == sponsor` in `Status.Active` with `totalEntries == 0`). It moves `unsettledPot` into `remainingRefundLiability`, zeroes `unsettledPot`, and sets `status = Status.Refunding`.

[Model: Raffle::refundTickets]
In `Status.Refunding`, a ticket owner passes a batch of 1 to 100 `ticketIds` they own. For each ticket, the contract checks `msg.sender == ownerOf(ticketId)`, sums `lastEntry - firstEntry + 1` from `_ticketRanges[ticketId]`, and burns `ticketId` (preventing duplicates in the same batch or future batches). It then decrements `remainingRefundLiability` by `aggregateEntries * 1,000,000` and transfers that USDC amount to `msg.sender`.

[Why: Raffle.sol:295]
Why does [`enableRefunds`](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol#L293-L297) allow `msg.sender == sponsor` to enable refunds before `endTime` when `totalEntries == 0`?
It rests on the belief that if no entries have been sold yet, the sponsor can cancel the raffle early and recover the escrowed NFT via `releaseSponsorPrize()` without harming any buyer.

[Defeat: Raffle::refundTickets]
1. Attacker passes duplicate `[ticketId, ticketId]` in `refundTickets(ticketIds)`. On index 0, `_burn(ticketId)` sets `_owners[ticketId] = address(0)`. On index 1, `ownerOf(ticketId)` calls `_requireOwned(ticketId)` which reverts with `ERC721NonexistentToken(ticketId)`.
2. Attacker buys a ticket with `entryCount = 1000` and refunds it; `refundTickets` bounds batch length by ticket count (`MAX_REFUND_TICKET_BATCH_SIZE = 100`) rather than entry count, so even a single ticket with a large `entryCount` refunds in O(1) gas.
3. Attacker mints or transfers a ticket to the predicted `CREATE` address of the next raffle clone `R2` before `R2` is deployed; once `R2` is deployed and `R1` enters `Status.Refunding`, `R2` cannot call `R1.refundTickets` and `_transferQuote(R2, amount)` would revert with `InvalidQuoteDestination(R2)` anyway, leaving `R2`'s refund permanently locked in `R1.remainingRefundLiability` while all other ticket holders can still refund their own tickets in full.

[LastOut: Lifecycle 5 — Refund Lifecycle]
When `enableRefunds()` executes, `remainingRefundLiability = unsettledPot = totalEntries * 1,000,000`. Because minted tickets `1 .. ticketCount` form an exact disjoint partition of `[1, totalEntries]`, the sum of `(lastEntry_i - firstEntry_i + 1) * 1,000,000` across all `ticketCount` tickets equals `totalEntries * 1,000,000 == remainingRefundLiability == quoteToken.balanceOf(address(this))`. Regardless of the order in which ticket owners call `refundTickets`, the last honest ticket owner out receives 100% of their entry payment (`entryCount * 1,000,000` USDC) with zero shortfall.

### Saturation Sweep

1. **Untrusted `prizeToken` & Decoupled Settlement vs. Prize Delivery (`_settleWinningTicket`, `releaseSponsorProceeds`, `redeemWinningTicket`)**:
   - Checked all payout functions in [Raffle.sol](file:///Users/hishamel-husseini/.codex/visualizations/2026/10/21/01a15d64-4430-7440-b259-192acf9762b5/raffle-audit-r001/runtime/gemini-native-repairs/SIMAO/attempt-04/leaf-workspaces/leaf-09/packages/contracts/src/Raffle.sol):
     - In `Status.CashWon`, the winner receives USDC (`winnerProceeds`) from trusted `quoteToken`, and the sponsor gets their own `prizeToken` back via `releaseSponsorPrize()`.
     - In `Status.Refunding`, ticket holders receive 100% USDC refunds from trusted `quoteToken`, and the sponsor gets their own `prizeToken` back via `releaseSponsorPrize()`.
     - In `Status.NftWon`, however, the winner's entire payout is the untrusted `prizeToken` (`redeemWinningTicket`), while the sponsor's payout is 95% of the USDC pot (`releaseSponsorProceeds`) and the treasury's payout is 5% of the USDC pot (`releaseProtocolFees`). Because `_settleWinningTicket` and `releaseSponsorProceeds` do not require `prizeClaimed == true` (i.e., successful delivery of the NFT to the winner in `redeemWinningTicket`), the sponsor can extract 95% of all buyers' USDC even when `prizeToken` is a malicious contract (explicitly declared untrusted in `DESIGN.md`) or a paused/expired ERC-721 that fails `redeemWinningTicket`.

```
FINDING | contract: Raffle | function: releaseSponsorProceeds | bug_class: trust-boundary-violation | group_key: Raffle | releaseSponsorProceeds | trust-boundary-violation
root_cause: In Raffle.sol:388, releaseSponsorProceeds() (and _settleWinningTicket() at Raffle.sol:546) allows releasing 95% of the USDC pot in Status.NftWon without requiring prizeClaimed == true, allowing a sponsor using an untrusted, paused, or expired prizeToken to withdraw 95% of buyer USDC while redeemWinningTicket() permanently reverts on prize delivery
internal_pre: Raffle resolves to Status.NftWon (totalEntries >= reserveEntries)
external_pre: prizeToken is either a malicious ERC-721 deployed by the sponsor (DESIGN.md specifies "arbitrary prize contracts and ticket recipients are untrusted") that blocks transfers after escrow, or an ERC-721 that expires/pauses during the raffle lifecycle
path:
  1. Sponsor deploys a prizeToken contract that returns true for supportsInterface(0x80ac58cd), accepts safeTransferFrom into the Raffle clone during createRaffle(reserveEntries = 10), and reverts on transferFrom when msg.sender == raffle and to != sponsorRecipient
  2. Honest buyers call buyEntries() for 10 entries, transferring 10,000,000 USDC (10 USDC) into Raffle (unsettledPot = 10,000,000)
  3. After endTime, requestDraw() and fulfillRandomWords() resolve the raffle to Status.NftWon
  4. Sponsor calls settleWinningTicket(winningTicketId) and releaseSponsorProceeds(), receiving 9,500,000 USDC (95% of the pot), while 500,000 USDC goes to protocolFees
  5. The winning ticket owner calls redeemWinningTicket(winningTicketId), which reverts in prizeToken.transferFrom(address(this), winner, deliveredPrizeTokenId) at Raffle.sol:347
impact: Ticket buyers lose 100% of their 10 USDC entry payments and the winning ticket owner is left holding an unredeemable winning ticket with neither the prize NFT nor any USDC recovery, while the sponsor walks away with 95% of the USDC pot (9.5 USDC) and retains control of the prize
mitigation: In Raffle.sol:388 (releaseSponsorProceeds) and Raffle.sol:398 (releaseProtocolFees), when status == Status.NftWon, require prizeClaimed == true before releasing sponsorProceeds and protocolFees, and allow transitioning from Status.NftWon to Status.Refunding if prizeClaimed remains false after a redemption/delivery deadline
```
